answer: A stake-and-slash reputation bond resists Sybil attacks: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove misbehavior. One identity costs little, but a vine of thousands of fake identities needs a gale of capital up front, and the attacker loses it all if any single node is caught. The umber shadow of fraud becomes too expensive to hide in, while honest agents earn their bond back with interest, so the cost falls only on attackers.
